The club 20-Miles Championship is down for decision on April 21st, and we would like all aspirants to our team for the "National" to shew their paces on this occasion. The "National" is on May 12th at Leicester, and some of the men we shall rely on to retrieve our lost honours are Cooper, Green, H.
Cooper (holder), and F. Rickards, who has been the winner on three occasions, for our 20 miles road-walking championship, on April 21st.

The club were placed third, with Green 7th, Cooper 10th, and Rickards 15th, in a field of 73. Only one team is entered for the National this year, and it includes Cooper, McMullen, Rickards, Green, H.
Cooper 10th, S.

Then, when the distination of the "Ricketts Shield" is to be settled upon, if "Tipster" did not welsh during the earlier race, he should be given the opportunity of quoting short prices concerning Green, McMullen, Cooper and King.

Starting in rather a narrow roadway the field was well bunched up for some 440 yards, where the first glimpse of our men was seen, and a hasty check showed Green 9th, McMullen 14th, Cooper 15th, Field 26th and Manning 47th.
…cture the finish of the Club 20 mile championship as a handicap with Field, Knifton and Saunders leading, and Green and Cooper at scratch vainly trying to catch them?…
Cooper, who is still one of our mainstays, was the 6th man to finish, but he had not then joined us. Windsor Park was the venue of the next race, and here we made our debut as National Champions.
The team that won in 1925 was: Rickards (2), Cooper (3), Wall (11), Hare (12). These figures are arrived at after eliminating the individual walkers.

The programme also included a 2 miles Team Walk to which we received an invitation, together with Woodford Green A.C., Enfield A.C., Highgate H., Surrey A.C. and the promoting club, Polytechnic H., Hyde, of Enfield, won, followed by Cooper and Pope, of Woodford Green, and Fletcher, of our Club.
Cooper, a fine runner, of T.V.H., won in good style, with Beswick, of Ashcombe A.C., second and Michael next. Our man ran rather green and will no doubt improve with more experience of scratch races.
Cooper and A.

Green, as expected, was the winner, being followed home by Sykes, Cooper and Watts, all of Eastleigh. Then came Harley and Bidgood, of ours, and as scoring was three aside, the home team won by 9 pts. to 12pts.
In the 2 miles walk we called upon Brown and Harley, to take on Cooper, Hake and Co., and in finishing 4th and 6th they did as well as could be expected.

Cooper, who had views on the five miles record, led; but seemed to lack the concentrated effort needed if records are to be broken. He was well outside Pope's figures at five miles, but continued for 9¼ miles, when he retired an obviously tired man.

One hundred and sixty-three competitors actually started to the signal of our President over our usual seven miles course, and from the start Johnson (Enfield), Cooper (Woodford Green), Redman (Metropolitan), Plumb (Enfield), Stone (Polytechnic) and Treacher, of ours, were prominent.

Don Brown had to give place to Cooper in the Walk, but his time of 13 min. 53.8 sec. is amazingly fast. Tommy Scrimshaw ran splendidly (he was unofficially timed at 1 min. 55.4 secs.) and yet this only gained fourth place.

Cooper. Special arrangements were made to have the track in really first-class condition, but these efforts were largely negatived by a torrential shower of rain just as proceedings were about to begin.

He was forced to yield to Cooper and Stone before the end was reached, but this effort of Harry's must rank as one of his best. Tommy Green, young as ever, and Len Fletcher, who we were all glad to see on the road once again, and Bill Treacher, completed our team.
Up to the half-distance the advantage was ours, but shortly afterwards Green, in attempting to race Cooper, was ruled out. This levelled matters, and the team fight was on.
Cooper's brilliance during the last year or so has rather dimmed Don's excellent performances, which some years would have given easy Championship wins.
In the Southern Championships held at Brighton, Brown was second to Cooper in the 2 miles Walk, and Bird finished fourth in the 880 yards, inside A.A.A. standard time.
The three miles event followed and in this Whitlock, Olympic Champion, and Cooper, A.A.A. champion, caused some excitement with the mixture of fast and slow walking they provided.
Cooper won once again, with E.
Dunford and Cooper have both tried long jumping, with some success, but our star in this event, Peverell, had the misfortunte to break his ankle early in the season.

Cooper and Stinton gained useful points in the high jump and Stinton was also third in the long jump. We were beaten by S.L.H. in the medley relay and the final scores were: S.L.H., 36 points; Belgrave, 33 points; Cambridge, 28 points.

Sinton did 5 ft. 6 in. last year and with Cooper, Jim Purdy (our best Western Roller), Steiner and Nettleton, we look really strong. We shall have to rely on Peter Sexton and Sinton for the Long Jump, but there are a number of others who could do well in this event if they really set their minds to it.

Cooper won both the Junior and Senior High Jump titles.
